name: Kingdom Teachings and Parables
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ
The Gospels and the Life of Christ

objectives.text: Identify a parable as a story Jesus told to teach about God and his kingdom
Retell the parable of the lost sheep and tell how the shepherd searched for the one that was lost
Retell the parable of the Good Samaritan and name the person who acted as a neighbor
Retell the parable of the prodigal son and describe how the father welcomed his son home
Recite the Lord's Prayer and identify the petition that asks for God's kingdom to come
State Jesus' announcement that the kingdom of God is at hand and his call to repent and believe the gospel
Compare the wise and foolish builders and explain what it means to hear and do Jesus' words
Identify the Golden Rule and give examples of how it applies in everyday situations
Explain the parable of the sower by matching each kind of soil to a way people respond to God's word
Describe the Beatitudes and explain the kind of people Jesus calls blessed in his kingdom
Explain what the parables of the mustard seed and the leaven teach about the small beginning and great growth of the kingdom
Explain what the parables of the hidden treasure and the pearl teach about the surpassing worth of the kingdom
Explain the meaning of each petition of the Lord's Prayer using the answers of the Westminster Shorter Catechism
Explain what the parable of the unforgiving servant teaches about forgiving others as God has forgiven us
Analyze how the audience and occasion of a parable shape its main point, using the grumbling Pharisees in Luke 15 as an example
Explain how Jesus teaches the full meaning of the law in the sayings of the Sermon on the Mount that begin you have heard that it was said
Analyze the theme of reversal in Jesus' kingdom teaching where the last are first and the humble are exalted
Analyze why Jesus taught in parables by explaining how they revealed the kingdom to disciples and concealed it from hardened hearers
Explain what the parables of the weeds, the ten virgins, the talents, and the sheep and goats teach about final judgment and readiness for Christ's return
Explain the cost of discipleship as Jesus teaches it through the tower builder and the king going to war
Explain the Reformed understanding of the kingdom of God as God's saving reign in Christ that advances through the word and Spirit
Evaluate competing interpretations of a parable by testing them against its literary context, its main point, and the rest of Scripture
Compose an essay explaining the ethic of the Sermon on the Mount and its relation to the law and to God's grace
Evaluate Jesus' command to love enemies in light of Old Testament law and the Reformed teaching on the sixth commandment
Defend Jesus' authority to interpret the law using the response of the crowds and his claim to fulfill the law and the prophets
Compare the parables of the Pharisee and tax collector and the laborers in the vineyard with the Reformed doctrine of justification by grace
Compare the Reformed view of the kingdom with views that reduce it to social reform or place it wholly in the future
Construct a synthesis of the already and not yet character of the kingdom drawn from Jesus' parables and kingdom sayings

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (identifying parables, Good Samaritan, prodigal son, wise and foolish builders, Golden Rule, sower, Beatitudes, Lord's Prayer, purpose of parables in Mark 4, cost of discipleship, Sermon on the Mount essay, loving enemies, Jesus' authority over the law, already and not yet). Replaced the vague 'observe Jesus taught about the kingdom' with Jesus' kingdom announcement in Mark 1:15 and moved 'upside-down kingdom' to a reversal-theme analysis with specific texts. Added missing kingdom parables (lost sheep, mustard seed and leaven, treasure and pearl, unforgiving servant, judgment parables), interpretive skills (audience and occasion, evaluating interpretations), the antitheses of Matthew 5, the Reformed doctrine of the kingdom, parables of grace and justification, and a comparison with other kingdom views. Corrected verse ranges and added catechism and confession anchors where they state the doctrine. Left miracles, nativity, and passion material to sibling sub-topics.
